business_summary: Starbucks is a global specialty coffee roaster and retailer with about 41,000 stores, 52% company-operated and 48% licensed, plus a Channel Development segment through the Nestle Global Coffee Alliance. North America is 74% of revenue. Fiscal 2025 revenue was $37.2B (+3%), with operating margin of 7.9% after restructuring, deleverage, labor investment and inflation. Key exposures are green coffee and dairy prices, store labor costs, comparable transactions and ticket, and store openings and closures.

pack_proposed.reason: Starbucks is a restaurant and retail beverage operator whose demand, menu pricing and store labor track US restaurant series.
pack_proposed.quote: Starbucks is the premier roaster, marketer, and retailer of specialty coffee in the world, operating in 89 markets.

drivers.reason: Green coffee is the primary commodity exposure; hedging and price-to-be-fixed contracts delay pass-through to costs, and purchase commitments are quantified.
drivers.quote: Commodity price risk represents our primary market risk, generated by our purchases of green coffee and dairy products, among other items.

kpis.name: store_operating_expense_pct_revenue
kpis.description: Store-related operating costs as a percent of revenue, reflecting labor deleverage.
kpis.reason: Store operating expenses rose 360 bps of revenue and drove margin contraction.
kpis.quote: Store operating expenses as a percentage of total net revenues increased 360 basis points.

kpis.name: product_distribution_cost_pct_revenue
kpis.description: Product and distribution costs as a percent of revenue.
kpis.reason: Captures coffee, dairy and tariff input cost inflation.
kpis.quote: Product and distribution costs as a percentage of total net revenues increased 50 basis points, primarily due to inflation (approximately 80 basis points).

edges.reason: Product and distribution costs include raw materials and are directly hit by commodity inflation.
edges.quote: The price and availability of these commodities, including impacts from volatility in green coffee prices and new tariffs, directly impact our results of operations, and we expect commodity prices, particularly coffee, to continue to impact future results of operations.

edges.reason: Wages and benefits are the largest store operating expense component.
edges.quote: Store operating expenses consist of costs incurred in our company-operated stores, primarily wages and benefits related to store partners (employees), occupancy costs, marketing, delivery commissions, and other costs that directly support the operation and sales-related activities of those stores.

edges.reason: Labor is one of the most significant costs and labor hours investment compressed margin.
edges.quote: Our business could be adversely impacted by increases in labor costs, including wages and benefits, which, in a retail business such as ours, are two of our most significant costs, both domestically and internationally.

edges.reason: Comparable transactions and ticket drive company-operated store revenue.
edges.quote: Comparable transactions declined 4%, partially offset by average ticket growth of 2%, primarily driven by annualization of pricing in the current year.

operating_kpis_suggested.name: comparable_store_sales_growth
operating_kpis_suggested.definition: Growth in sales at company-operated stores open 13 months or longer, excluding FX.
operating_kpis_suggested.quote: Comparable store sales includes company-operated stores open 13 months or longer, and exclude the effects of foreign currency exchange rates.

operating_kpis_suggested.name: comparable_transactions
operating_kpis_suggested.definition: Change in comparable store transaction count, a traffic measure, by segment.
operating_kpis_suggested.quote: Comparable transactions declined 4%, partially offset by average ticket growth of 2%, primarily driven by annualization of pricing in the current year.

operating_kpis_suggested.name: store_count
operating_kpis_suggested.definition: Net new company-operated and licensed stores by market, net of closures.
